articles.title: 'It's pretty toxic… but just a little, I want to be like that': What young men think of manosphere content
articles.dek: by Krista Fisher, Emily Lewis, Vivian Gerrand, Zac Seidler, The Conversation
paragraphs: by Krista Fisher, Emily Lewis, Vivian Gerrand, Zac Seidler, The Conversation

Masculinity content promises young men self-optimization and success, but often delivers health harms, risk-taking, unattainable standards, gender stereotypes and misogyny. The latter is the strongest predictor of violent extremism .
Policymakers, advocates, teachers and parents are all calling for change. But young men are often absent from these conversations and calls for solutions .
Our new research brings their perspectives into the story.

We asked 142 young men ages 16 to 25 in Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States what they think and how they make sense of masculinity content on social media. Their verdict: "Some of it's fucked, some of it's useful."

These young men described being pulled in multiple directions and valuing practical self-help advice. At the same time, they critiqued "toxic" messages about masculinity and health behaviors that harm men, women and marginalized groups.
Like most wellness content online, masculinity content manufactures insecurities and sells solutions through self-optimization.

Finance, fitness and dating advice all promise to make young men desirable, confident and successful. Some felt it genuinely helped. Kieran, a 24-year-old from the U. K. , said, "I am looking for the lessons and takeaways that can have a positive impact if I implement them in my life. And I ignore the rest. Overall, I like it. It has helped with my self-confidence and has helped me with discipline and exercise."

Masculinity content offered support that young men didn't get elsewhere. For some, it was a roadmap to the kind of success they equated with self-worth: financial security, a partner, a successful career and a fit physique.

But many simultaneously saw a darker side. They called out unsustainable lifestyles, influencers exploiting young men's insecurities and superficial content that could not provide young men with real, long-term well-being.

Andy, a 22-year-old Australian man, said, "It's pretty toxic but at the same time I can't help but want the confidence that their methods seem to provide. Like I don't want to be a part of it because it's messed up, but just a little I want to be like that so I feel respected or at least deserving of it."
Even though they were not asked about it specifically, the majority of young men referenced the manosphere and manfluencers, such as self-described misogynist Andrew Tate.
Some endorsed restrictive and oppressive models of masculinity and traditional gender roles in relationships and families, equating these with the type of man they wanted to become.

But many more disliked the promotion of misogyny, violence, risk-taking and health harms they saw online. A 19-year-old named Cam told us, "It's fairly 50/50. A good portion of the content is focused on masculinity without scrutinizing women. Whereas I feel that the louder minority latch on to overly masculine role models who promote the idea that in order to be a successful male, you have to belittle women."

articles.title: Scientists demonstrate AI-designed enzyme for drug synthesis
articles.dek: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate…
paragraphs: The new RFD4-Proteina unified generative model for protein design—created by the Institute for Protein Design (IPD) in collaboration with NVIDIA—uses advanced AI to generate entirely new protein sequences and structures, achieving computational design success rates five to 10 times higher than previous models and generating candidates five to 10 times faster.

AI-based protein design is already transforming protein science, but RFD4-Proteina differs in how it tackles the design problem. The model can consider several interconnected aspects of structure and function simultaneously, refining a protein's amino-acid sequence and three-dimensional structure alongside the molecules with which it interacts. It can also direct more computational effort toward promising designs, helping researchers identify candidates with specific functions more efficiently.

Researchers at The University of Manchester's Manchester Institute of Biotechnology (MIB), including professor Anthony Green, Dr. Henry Jones and Dr. Zefei Xu, worked in collaboration with IPD to apply RFD4-Proteina to design de novo enzymes for low-cost and sustainable production of global health drugs.

One of the team's most significant tests focused on the synthesis of lenacapavir , a drug used for HIV prevention. RFD4-Proteina was used to design entirely new enzymes capable of catalyzing a key amide-bond-forming reaction involved in the drug's synthesis. Of the 67 designs selected for experimental testing, four showed clear activity, with the best converting 79% of a bulky chiral amine into the desired amide product.

The enzyme also displays high selectivity for the S- enantiomer of the amine as required for the lenacapavir synthesis. This reaction is particularly challenging because the enzyme must favor the desired amide-bond-forming process while suppressing a competing reaction with water, which is present in a vast excess in enzyme-mediated transformations.

This research, available as a preprint , represents a critical proof-of-concept demonstration that new enzymes can be designed computationally to promote challenging steps in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

"It was a pleasure to work with the IPD team to road-test the new RFD4-Proteina model on a highly complex and valuable enzyme design challenge. The initial results are spectacular and show how these advanced models can rapidly deliver new biocatalysts for producing therapeutics and other essential chemicals," said Green, director of the MIB.

Proteins are essential for life and perform a wide range of functions. For example, enzymes speed up chemical reactions involved in metabolism, while antibodies bind to pathogens to help fight infection. Proteins are also important in manufacturing chemicals and materials used in everyday products, including medicines and fuels. But designing new functional proteins such as enzymes is difficult.

Enzymes found in nature have traditionally provided the starting point for scientists seeking to engineer biocatalysts with useful functions. More recently, computational protein design has made it possible to design completely new proteins. However, this remains difficult as scientists must find a combination of amino-acid sequence, three-dimensional structure and molecular interactions capable of performing the intended task from an enormous number of possibilities.

Developed by professor David Baker and his team at the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design (IPD), RFD4-Proteina was designed to address this problem. It combines two existing AI models—the IPD's RosettaFold Diffusion line and Proteina-Complexa from NVIDIA—allowing scientists to design brand new proteins with a specified function, focusing laboratory testing on a handful of the most promising candidates.

"RFD4-Proteina will open the door to new solutions in medicine, sustainability, materials and biotechnology," said Baker, IPD director and professor of biochemistry at the University of Washington School of Medicine. Baker is a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator and a recipient of the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry.

RFD4-Proteina's biomolecular reasoning is novel; it learns the "language" of existing proteins by training on a large data set, and tests in silico a huge number of design possibilities to fit a desired function.

Like language models with adjustable "thinking," RFD4-Proteina can devote more computation to difficult problems. It concurrently refines a protein's sequence and structure alongside the structures of interacting molecules, so that a change in one seamlessly informs changes in the others.

articles.title: Chemically modified sugars enable direct nanostructure formation
articles.dek: by National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology
paragraphs: by National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

Researchers at AIST have demonstrated the synthesis of nanoporous carbonaceous materials and carbonaceous materials with layered nanostructures through a simple process involving the chemical modification of common sugars such as sucrose and fructose.

Nanoporous carbonaceous materials have attracted attention as materials that can help address energy-related challenges, with potential applications as catalyst supports and electrode materials for secondary batteries. In particular, carbonaceous materials with highly uniform pore sizes and shapes, which can be tailored for specific applications, are in increasing demand.

The conventional templating method, however, has several drawbacks, including the need for sacrificial template agents and complex synthesis procedures that consume resources and generate waste. Furthermore, some templating procedures rely on energy-intensive and harsh chemical processes involving high temperatures and strong acids.

A research group at AIST has developed a new method that enables the synthesis of nanostructured carbonaceous materials solely from chemically modified sugar molecules. The method uses sugar molecules modified to bear an alkyl chain as carbon precursors. These precursors are subjected to hydrothermal treatment, during which condensation reactions take place.
This approach provides access to nanostructured carbonaceous materials without relying on conventional templates or harsh chemical processing.

Furthermore, the nanostructure of the resulting carbonaceous material can be altered by varying the type of sugar headgroup, yielding either a nanoporous carbonaceous material with spherical nanopores or a carbonaceous material with a layered nanoscale structure.

This work represents a shift from the current "physical" pore formation pathway based on the templating method to a "chemical" pore formation pathway. The researchers expect that the method will serve as a synthesis platform for designing novel nanoporous carbonaceous materials with nanostructural features that are inaccessible through conventional templating methods.
Using such materials as scaffolds for various chemical reactions may improve material performance in applications such as electrodes and catalyst supports.
Details of this research were published online in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on Aug. 12, 2026.

Nanoporous carbonaceous materials have numerous nanoscale pores and a large specific surface area and have been widely recognized for their ability to store electricity, adsorb substances and promote chemical reactions. For example, in application studies involving energy storage and fuel cells, nanoporous carbonaceous materials provide a platform for charge storage processes as well as various chemical reactions.

Activated carbon, a widely known porous carbonaceous material, is used for water purification and deodorization due to its high porosity, which allows it to capture molecules of various sizes. However, its pore size and shape are normally not uniform.

In contrast, porous carbonaceous materials with pores that are uniform in size and shape can also capture molecules of specific sizes, offering advantages for applications such as energy storage, gas separation and catalysis. This capability has accelerated demand for nanoporous carbonaceous materials that have uniform pore structures and are suitable for these applications.

articles.title: The psychology of why we overpay for used cars—study points to left-digit bias
articles.dek: Consumers routinely ignore information when making purchases.
paragraphs: Consumers routinely ignore information when making purchases. They overlook the tax attached to a price, skim past ingredient lists and often fail to process exact numbers with any precision.
This kind of inattention is well documented. What is less well understood is how businesses exploit this behavior.

Assistant professor Andreas Kraft of the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and University of Texas professor Raghunath Rao explored a specific form of inattention known as left-digit bias, which is among the most reliably documented quirks in consumer psychology. Their study, focused on the used-car market, suggests that dealerships systematically attract more inattentive buyers and profit handsomely as a result—and also that this bias could be hard to address with increased disclosure or transparency.

Consumers anchor heavily on the leftmost digit when they evaluate a number. Prices such as $1. 99 or $1. 90 exploit this tendency. Left-digit bias, and the fact that people possess it in varying degrees, creates a distinct dynamic in the used-car market.

Inattentive buyers at a dealership see a car with 49,800 miles (80,100 kilometers) and mentally register something closer to 40,000 miles (64,400 kilometers). That misperception inflates both what they think the car is worth and what they think they would pay for an equivalent car in the private market, the researchers explain.

Their study analyzed prices and odometer readings in every title submission to the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles between 2014 and 2021—a data set that captured roughly 10% of all vehicle transactions in the United States during this period. Inattentive buyers tend to purchase used cars from dealerships rather than private sellers, according to the researchers, who add that dealers are generally more aware of left-digit bias and able to capitalize on it.

Dealerships always command a premium over private markets but charge even more for cars near favorable mileage thresholds. To inattentive buyers, those prices can still appear attractive because they perceive the car as having lower mileage than it really does and therefore overestimate what a comparable car would cost elsewhere.

Attentive buyers, by contrast, more accurately determine what a 49,800-mile (80,100-kilometer) car should cost, recognize the dealership premium and go elsewhere. Kraft and Rao find that dealership customers, based on the prices they paid, were about twice as inattentive to exact mileage as customers who shopped in the private market.
This sorting mechanism has clear financial consequences.

In a process the researchers call "behavioral skimming," dealerships charged significantly more for vehicles with odometer readings just below a 10,000-mile (16,100-kilometer) threshold than for comparable cars just above. Kraft and Rao find the difference in profit ranged from roughly $46 to $168 per vehicle across the various thresholds, with the sharpest effects between 60,000 miles (96,600 kilometers) and 100,000 miles (160,900 kilometers), where the bulk of dealership transactions occurred.

For the 14 cutoffs they examined between 10,000 miles (16,100 kilometers) and 140,000 miles (225,300 kilometers), the average profit on vehicles 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers) below the threshold was nearly 11% higher than profit on vehicles 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometers) above the threshold.

And while raising prices reduces sales volume in most markets, the opposite occurred in this setting. Because the elevated price attracted a pool of inattentive buyers willing to pay, dealerships bid more aggressively on the supply side.

Vehicles with odometer readings just below a 10,000-mile (16,100-kilometer) threshold were up to 4% more likely to be sold through a dealership than in the private market. They also sold faster. Cars just below 90,000 miles (144,800 kilometers) spent about two fewer days on the lot than those just above, translating to 6% less time in inventory. These lower inventory costs on top of higher margins compounded the benefits.

Competition between dealers didn't erode this advantage, as standard economic models suggest it should. Conversely, the researchers find, inattention among dealership customers was 40% higher in the most competitive markets (as measured by inventory levels) compared with the least competitive markets.

articles.title: Designing better adsorbents to remove PFAS from water
articles.dek: A review by Tohoku University researchers identifies key molecular features that could guide the development of more effective materials for removing PFAS from water.
paragraphs: A review by Tohoku University researchers identifies key molecular features that could guide the development of more effective materials for removing PFAS from water. The study is published in the journal ACS Materials Au .

Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are used in a wide range of industries, from semiconductor manufacturing and firefighting to textiles and food packaging. Their chemical stability and ability to repel water and oil make them useful in many applications. However, concerns about the potential health effects of some PFAS have increased the need for effective ways to remove these chemicals from water.

One promising approach is adsorption , in which PFAS molecules attach to the surface of a material called an adsorbent. By tailoring these materials to interact with specific PFAS molecules, researchers aim to improve their ability to capture these persistent chemicals from water.

A research team led by Kouki Oka, associate professor at Tohoku University's Institute of Multidisciplinary Research for Advanced Materials, reviewed current research and development in PFAS adsorption. The review examines well-studied compounds, including perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), alongside other PFAS covered by regulatory and monitoring frameworks in the European Union (EU) and Canada. The team identifies key principles for designing high-performance adsorbents that can target a wider range of PFAS.

A central finding is that effective adsorbent design requires understanding the different parts of a PFAS molecule. PFOS and PFOA, for example, each contain a fluorinated carbon chain and a terminal group that is typically charged in aqueous environments. These parts have different chemical properties and can interact with adsorbent materials in different ways.

By designing materials that interact strongly with these different structural features, researchers may be able to improve adsorption performance. Rather than treating a PFAS molecule as a single target, this approach considers its individual components to guide the selection and design of suitable adsorbents.

"As the range of PFAS subject to regulation continues to expand, we need adsorbents that can effectively target a wider variety of these compounds. By understanding how different parts of PFAS molecules interact with adsorbent materials, we can establish clearer design principles for developing more effective removal technologies," says Oka.

The need for such materials is growing as governments expand PFAS monitoring and regulation. In the EU, drinking water standards set a limit of 100 nanograms per liter (ng/L) for the combined concentration of 20 PFAS. The EU has also established environmental quality standards for 25 PFAS in surface waters, with an annual average limit of 4. 4 ng/L expressed as PFOA equivalents to account for differences in toxicity. Canada has set an objective of 30 ng/L for the combined concentration of 25 PFAS.

As more PFAS come under regulatory scrutiny, removal technologies will need to address a broader range of molecular structures. The design principles outlined in this review provide a foundation for developing adsorbents tailored to different PFAS, potentially improving water treatment and helping industries manage these persistent chemicals.
The research team's next step is to apply these principles to the development of higher-performance adsorbents designed for specific PFAS.

articles.title: Plain silicon grating reveals a hidden 'twist' in light from electron beams
articles.dek: In 1953, two physicists showed that an electron beam skimming past a grating emits light whose color depends only on the electron's speed and the grating's spacing.
paragraphs: In 1953, two physicists showed that an electron beam skimming past a grating emits light whose color depends only on the electron's speed and the grating's spacing. Known as Smith-Purcell radiation, this phenomenon has become a useful tool for building compact, tunable light sources and tracking particle beams without touching them.

Now, researchers from Singapore and China have discovered that this well-studied effect has been hiding a property nobody thought to look for: chirality, or "handedness." In their paper "Observation of inherent chiral Smith-Purcell effect via symmetry breaking," published in Nature Communications , associate professors Wu Lin and Dong Zhaogang from the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) showed that the radiation is inherently chiral and demonstrated two simple ways to bring that chirality out with a plain silicon grating.

"The main reason it was missed is symmetry," said Wu. "The chirality was always there, but the left- and right-handed components are distributed symmetrically in space. In conventional measurements, we usually look only along the symmetry plane, so the two opposite contributions cancel each other."

A moving electron drags a twisting electromagnetic field around it, and a grating can convert this into circularly polarized light. In three-dimensional simulations, the emission is left-handed on one side of the beam, right-handed on the other, and linearly polarized in the middle, the only place earlier two-dimensional models had looked.

To tip the scales, the researchers broke the symmetry in two ways: by rotating the grating relative to the electron beam, or by keeping the grating fixed and moving the beam from the center toward one edge. "Twisting lets us tune the chirality, while shifting lets us select a stable handedness over a broad wavelength range," added Dong.

Both approaches were tested on silicon gratings inside a scanning electron microscope, with the emitted light sorted into left- and right-handed parts. On the standard scale, where 1 means purely one-handed light and 0 means no net handedness, the measured value climbed with the twist angle to 0. 726 at 30 degrees. Reversing the twist flipped the handedness.

Shrinking the grating pitch from 120 to 100 nanometers pushed the value to 0. 87, the highest yet reported for Smith-Purcell radiation and more than double the previous best. Shifting the beam gave one handedness along one edge and the opposite along the other, and simulations predict values of up to 0. 98.
"The key insight was that we did not need to make the silicon grating itself chiral," noted Dong. "The chirality was already hidden in the electromagnetic field carried by the moving electrons."

The shifting experiments gave the researchers a surprise. The emission was strongest with the electron beside the grating rather than above it, because the sharp corners of the grating scatter the electron's field into light remarkably well.

"Once we understood the role of the grating edge, the result made physical sense," Dong shared. "It showed us that where the electron travels relative to the structure can be just as important as the structure itself."

As neither approach relies on a delicate optical resonance, the effect is naturally broadband. The emitted light could be tuned from about 450 to 900 nanometers while the chirality changed only slightly. Avoiding resonance also promises simpler fabrication and greater freedom in choosing materials. Wu sees chiral light sources as the application closest to practical use, with extreme ultraviolet light—prized in lithography—an attractive target.

However, challenges remain. Materials must be chosen carefully, since some glow under electron bombardment and can swamp the signal. Reaching X-ray wavelengths would demand even smaller structures or much higher electron energies, and quantum effects may then complicate the picture.

"The challenge is not as simple as generating X-rays," Dong said. "It is to generate them while preserving and controlling their chirality, and to understand the new quantum physics that may emerge at these much smaller scales."

Nonetheless, these findings point to a new way of designing free-electron light sources. Said Wu, "Instead of making the structure increasingly complicated, we can create new functionality by controlling the symmetry of the electron-structure interaction."

articles.title: Ancestors all around – millions of dead people linger in Americans’ memories
articles.dek: Halloween kicks off a series of religious and cultural festivals to honor the dead, including All Saints’ Day, All Souls’ Day and the Day of the Dead.
paragraphs: Halloween kicks off a series of religious and cultural festivals to honor the dead, including All Saints’ Day, All Souls’ Day and the Day of the Dead. But deceased loved ones don’t disappear from people’s social worlds once the ghost and skeleton decorations come down.

Present in memory and tradition, the dead can shape people’s identities and behaviors long after they die. Recent survey data shows that almost 44% of Americans report that they have felt the presence of a deceased relative or that they have communicated with a deceased relative in the past year alone.

Researchers lack basic knowledge about this shadow population. As demographers , we typically study the living. But in our recent work, we asked a very unusual demographic question: What does a population of our deceased relatives look like?

Our research typically categorizes the living population by age groups and other demographic attributes. In our recent study, we took our analysis a step further to estimate the size and age distribution of the currently living population’s deceased relatives. We focused specifically on deceased grandparents, parents, siblings, spouses and children.

To do this project, we relied on a modeling framework called demographic microsimulations . This approach produces results only for Black and white Americans. The method cannot estimate relative populations living outside of the United States, so it excludes groups with high percentages of foreign-born individuals who have family abroad.
Our study focused on the populations as of July 2020, but for the purposes of this article, we updated our analysis and weighted results to the estimated population as of October 2026.

Because estimating the deceased relative population is not a common exercise in our field, we had to make some modeling decisions. We counted only deceased relatives who died after the birth of at least one person still alive; if no one remains who could remember them, we did not include them.

Also, we counted deceased persons based on how many relatives they have in the living population. For example, if a deceased 60-year-old man is survived by a spouse, an adult child, a grandchild and a sibling, we count him in the deceased relative population four times, reflecting his being remembered by four living individuals. As such, the deceased relative population we quantified is really a count of how many direct relative ties remain to those who are dead.

And finally, we classified deceased relatives according to their age at death. We believe this represents the age many people will most clearly remember their deceased loved ones. Of course, we categorize the living population by their current age.

First, the deceased relative population is large. Our model estimated that the living Black and white populat,ion representing about 217 million people , had 755 million ties to deceased close relatives . That’s a population more than three times the size of the living population. For every under-15-year-old out trick-or-treating on Halloween, there are about 21 deceased relatives remembered.

Second, our model shows that, on average, the deceased relatives died 25 years ago. That the average deceased relative has been remembered for a quarter of a century makes it clear that loved ones are often suspended in memory for years, even decades, after their deaths.

Third, over half of the deceased relative population was born more than 100 years ago – even before the term “trick-or-treating” took hold in the U. S . Around 10% of the deceased relatives were born before 1900, with 140,000 of them born before the Civil War – these are the remembered grandparents of today’s oldest individuals. These results speak to how generations of the seemingly long ago past still have a direct tie to the living.

The Halloween season reminds us of ghosts, spirits and ancestors. Whatever their beliefs, many Americans also carry relationships with people who are no longer alive: grandparents whose recipes they still make, parents whose advice they still hear, spouses whose absence shapes their days.

These relationships are deeply personal, but together they form a vast and previously unstudied shadow population. By quantifying and characterizing the deceased relative population, our research reveals just how many people no longer appear in the census yet remain an integral part of our social world.

articles.title: UN peacekeepers prepare to exit Lebanon after 70 years – leaving behind a worrying security vacuum
articles.dek: For nearly 70 years, the blue helmets of United Nations’ peacekeepers have dotted the landscape of southern Lebanon. But those days may soon be over.
paragraphs: For nearly 70 years, the blue helmets of United Nations’ peacekeepers have dotted the landscape of southern Lebanon. But those days may soon be over.
Under Israeli and American pressure, the U. N. Security Council unanimously voted in August to end the mandate establishing the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon, or UNIFIL .
It means the 7,565 members of UNIFIL deployed in Lebanon – representing about 46 countries – will depart the country no later than Dec. 31, 2026.

The end of the U. N. presence comes at a pivotal time. Israel and Lebanon have already held seven rounds of negotiations aimed at bringing a lasting peace to a region that has suffered from decades of conflict.

Brokered by the United States, these talks that led to the signing of the Trilateral Framework in June 2026 call for the disarmament of Hezbollah, the Israeli withdrawal from all Lebanese lands and the settlement of all disputes over borders. Yet all of these conditions are still some way off from completion – and beset by a series of barriers .

As such, the departure of the United Nations peacekeeping forces raises serious concerns. The potential for a security vacuum looms large in south Lebanon, especially given that Israel continues to bomb Lebanon despite a ceasefire that has nominally been in place since April 16, 2026 .

As a scholar of Middle East Studies , I know that UNIFIL has never been a permanent solution. But I fear that its termination creates more problems than it solves, especially when there are no clear replacements or post-UNIFIL security arrangements in place.
While the U. N. had had an on-the-ground presence in Lebanon to handle civil strife since the 1950s , its role in mediating between Lebanon and Israel started later.

In 1978, after a series of attacks on Israel organized by Palestinian fighters in Lebanon, Israel invaded and occupied the south in what was known as Operation Litani . As a result, the United Nations Security Council established UNIFIL to monitor Israel’s withdrawal from south Lebanon and to restore peace at the Lebanese–Israeli border.

Israel’s occupation of south Lebanon lasted more than two decades . Following its withdrawal on May 25, 2000, the U. N. set the Blue Line – a 75-mile (120 km) demarcation line created for the practical purpose of confirming Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon. It was not an official border but a buffer zone monitored by the U. N. peacekeepers.
UNFIL and the Blue Line served as geographic and diplomatic focal points in the 2006 war between Hezbollah – an Iranian-backed militia operating from Lebanon – and Israel.

Resolution 1701 of the Security Council, which brought an end to the 2006 war, dramatically expanded the UNIFIL role in Lebanon ; the number of troops went from 2,000 to 15,000 authorized military personnel.

Its mandate also changed to include monitoring the ceasefire and documenting its violations, coordinating with Lebanon’s military and functioning as the only direct communication channel between the Lebanese and Israeli militaries. UNIFIL also offered humanitarian aid to the affected civilian population of south Lebanon.

Yet UNIFIL’s role never altered the basic lack of peace on the Israeli-Lebanese border. Over 50 years, Israel invaded Lebanon numerous times . And since 2000, Hezbollah has flourished in south Lebanon .

As UNIFIL prepares to depart, it’s unclear what will fill the looming security vacuum. It could be filled by non-U. N. troops, but Lebanon’s past shows the risks inherent to international peacekeeping missions.

In 1982, after Israel invaded Lebanon and occupied Beirut with the intention of eliminating the Palestinian militant threat, Lebanese authorities called on Western powers for help. In August, the governments of the U. S. , France, Italy and the United Kingdom created a multinational peacekeeping force designed to restore peace and stop the fighting between the Lebanese, Palestinians and Israelis.
But on Oct. 23, 1983 , the multinational peacekeeping force was the target of a dual suicide attack that killed 241 American service members and 58 French paratroopers.
To this day, the attack – claimed by the pro-Iranian Islamic Jihad – remains the deadliest single-day incident for the U. S. Marine Corps since the Battle of Iwo Jima in 1945.
In addition to Israel, interventions in Lebanon have also come from another neighboring country.

In 1976, the Syrian military intervened during Lebanon’s civil war to put an end to sectarian violence. Nearly three decades of occupation followed, and troops were withdrawn only following the assassination of Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik Hariri in 2005 and the subsequent Cedar Revolution .
With the absence of an internal Lebanese consensus, the arrival of any international peacekeeping force to replace the exiting UNIFIL will be perceived by many Lebanese as a top-down imposition.

Moreover, the situation on the ground makes it dangerous for any international force to successfully operate. Israel is reportedly occupying over 10% of Lebanon’s territories , including multiple permanent bases and outposts in southern Lebanese territory.
Finally, the fate of Lebanon-Israel direct negotiations is unclear . Recently, the countries held military talks in Florida, but little is expected from them .

Yet a number of efforts are ongoing despite the difficult circumstances surrounding UNIFIL’s withdrawal. On June 25, French President Emmanuel Macron and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced an “ international coalition to support Lebanon ” to reinforce Lebanon’s sovereignty and help prevent a security vacuum in south Lebanon.

articles.title: Researchers Find an Unexpected Benefit of Putting Sheep on Solar Farms
articles.dek: Solar grazing is helping sheep farmers expand their businesses, opening opportunities for rural jobs, new investment, and stronger agricultural supply chains.
paragraphs: Solar grazing is helping sheep farmers expand their businesses, opening opportunities for rural jobs, new investment, and stronger agricultural supply chains.

Sheep can feed on the vegetation growing around solar panels while farmers get paid to keep it under control. Too few sheep may leave farmers with grass they still need to mow, while heavier grazing can reduce honeybee numbers.

Two new Cornell University studies examine the ecological and financial choices behind this growing practice, known as solar grazing. One tested how the number of sheep on the land affects beneficial insects. The other developed a tool to help farmers plan flock size, purchases, and sales.

At two sheep per hectare, or roughly one per 1. 2 acres, the combined abundance of wild bees, honey bees, and lady beetles was 38% higher than in a mowed control plot. Honey bee numbers were 83% higher, accounting for most of the overall increase.

Doubling the density to four sheep per hectare improved vegetation control, but beneficial insect abundance was similar to that in the mowed control. Eight sheep per hectare delivered the strongest vegetation control, and flock health remained high. At that density, however, honey bee abundance fell by 45%.

“We zeroed in on stocking rates because that’s a concrete number that sheep farmers understand and work with every day, and we want this research to be useful,” said Steve Grodsky, the study’s senior author and an assistant professor of natural resources in Cornell’s Ashley School of Global Development and the Environment. “With solar grazing, people, energy, agricultural animals, plants, and insects are all part of this ecosystem. We’re trying to understand the connections between those pieces so that when solar developers, municipalities looking at solar development, or farmers are faced with a decision, they can have scientific information about potential trade-offs and synergies.”

The researchers spent three years testing those stocking rates, the number of sheep grazing a given area, at the university-owned Cascadilla Community Solar Farm in Dryden, New York. Using Cornell’s teaching flock, the team brought together entomologists, ecologists, and animal and plant scientists from the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS). Their paper was published in Environmental Research Letters .

“Sheep grazing and beneficial insect habitat are two prominent conversation topics around solar development right now,” said Leana Zoller, the paper’s first author and a postdoctoral associate in natural resources in the Ashley School. “But what’s been missing is research that treats them as parts of the same system. When we talk about sustainable solar development, integrating these discussions into a single framework is really helpful to farmers and community decision makers.”

Grodsky also serves as assistant unit leader of the U. S. Geological Survey New York Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit. Sarah Carson, director of Cornell’s Campus Sustainability Office, helped coordinate the researchers’ access to the site with the solar company responsible for managing it.

The study’s other CALS co-authors included sheep farmer and solar grazing consultant Nikola Kochendoerfer, Ph. D. ’20, Antonio DiTommaso, a professor in the School of Integrative Plant Science, and John Losey, a professor of entomology. Also contributing were Scott McArt, Ph. D. ’12, an associate professor of entomology, Paige Muñiz, formerly a technician in McArt’s lab, and Todd Ugine, Ph. D. ’04, a research associate in Losey’s lab.

For farmers deciding how many sheep to buy or sell, the second study offers a way to weigh the financial and practical demands together. Researchers led from the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business developed a spreadsheet-based model that uses target flock size, costs, anticipated revenue, and expected vegetation at individual solar sites to help optimize those decisions. They presented the tool in a separate study published in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management .

Solar developers can also use the model to understand what farmers need from a grazing agreement and design contracts that are more profitable and sustainable for everyone involved over the long term. United Agrivoltaics has already made the tool part of its onboarding process.

articles.title: Scientists Discover a New Butterfly Species Hiding in Plain Sight
articles.dek: Nearly identical butterflies share the same tropical forests, yet scientists still cannot fully explain how they recognize their own kind.
paragraphs: Nearly identical butterflies share the same tropical forests, yet scientists still cannot fully explain how they recognize their own kind.

When Andrés Orellana found caterpillars stripping the leaves from a Cecropia sapling in Venezuela, they had the familiar black bodies and yellow spines of Colobura butterflies. None, however, had the cream-colored markings seen in the two known species.

That missing detail helped lead researchers to a third species, Colobura cryptica . Anisha Sapkota, a doctoral student at the Florida Museum of Natural History, and her colleagues described the species in Zootaxa , drawing on genetic evidence and subtle differences in the insects’ appearance. Their work also raised an unresolved question about how these nearly identical butterflies remain separate species while sharing much of the same territory.

Colobura is a familiar presence in the tropical Americas, or neotropics. These rainforests are among the most biodiverse places on Earth. Costa Rica alone supports half a million species, five times as many as Canada on roughly one two-hundredth of its land area.
“If you go to the neotropics, Colobura is one of the first butterflies you see,” Sapkota said.

Their caterpillars feed on Cecropia , trees as characteristic of these tropical forests as balsam firs are of boreal forests in parts of Canada. In 1888, German botanist Andreas Schimper wrote, “Every naturalist who has been in tropical America will remember Cecropia , belonging to the most conspicuous trees of those countries.”

Both the butterflies and their host trees occur across a broad area that includes parts of the Andes, the Brazilian Amazon, the Atlantic Rainforest in Brazil and Paraguay, and much of Central America and the Caribbean. Most of the 61 Cecropia species occupy only part of that territory, with some restricted to the Andes and others to the Caribbean. For more than two centuries after Carl Linnaeus’s 1758 description, however, scientists recognized just one widespread species of Colobura , called C. dirce .

The caterpillars offered an early reason to question that classification. Their velvety black bodies carry bright yellow stalks tipped with sharp, angled barbs, a warning that roughly translates to “leave me alone, or there will be unpleasant consequences.” Beneath the spines, some have cream-colored teardrops, while others have rings. In 1852, Dutch entomologist Jan Sepp argued that these different markings distinguished two species. His peers dismissed the idea, and for roughly the next 150 years, naturalists attributed the differences to variation between males and females or among individuals of the same species.

Keith Willmott, now a curator at the Florida Museum’s McGuire Center for Lepidoptera and Biodiversity, later helped revisit that interpretation. He explained why even recognizing a second species had seemed difficult to accept.
“It’s a very distinctive butterfly. It’s hard to imagine there being two species in the same area that look alike because they’re so different from anything else.”
In 2001, Willmott and several colleagues revived Sepp’s idea and formally described Colobura annulata . “We assumed that was the problem solved,” Willmott said. He moved on to other projects.

About a quarter century later, Orellana’s photographs of the unmarked Venezuelan caterpillars gave Willmott enough evidence to reopen the investigation. Orellana was one of his colleagues, and the photographs brought him back to a possibility he had previously set aside. “I had a few indications that there was a third species, but I thought it was too implausible.”

Sapkota had just joined the Florida Museum’s Shirey lab and expressed interest in leading the work. To investigate the butterflies’ genetic relationships, she analyzed highly variable stretches of DNA known as barcodes. These sequences had been collected and curated through a long-term survey of Lepidoptera, the group that includes butterflies and moths, in Costa Rica. Study co-authors Daniel Janzen and Winnie Hallwachs led that survey.

Building on the barcode results, Sapkota sent older museum specimens collected throughout the neotropics to Nick Grishin at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center. Grishin sequenced their mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. Together, the DNA analyses identified three distinct lineages that matched the physical differences the researchers documented.

articles.title: NASA, Virginia Launch Power Partnership for Energy Security
articles.dek: NASA is helping to foster long-term energy security in Virginia.
paragraphs: NASA is helping to foster long-term energy security in Virginia.

NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, is partnering with the Virginia Department of Energy to support informed decisions for effective energy generation, delivery and use by providing solar, meteorological, and future weather risk datasets for energy system modeling and planning purposes.

Under a new Space Act Agreement announced during a ceremony Friday, the partnership will use NASA expertise in atmospheric sciences to assist Virginia Energy in support of resiliency studies, resource analysis, and long-term energy planning.

“NASA Langley relishes the opportunity to put our unique science data into the hands of those who want to improve people’s lives,” said NASA Langley Deputy Director Allen Kilgore. “This collaboration with Virginia Energy will benefit the citizens of Virginia and provide stronger energy security for the Commonwealth.”

This agreement will help state officials plan for current and potential extreme weather conditions in Virginia and assess implications for electricity demand, energy generation, and system stress. Information can be directly incorporated into energy policy, planning, and operational decisions.

By helping Virginians better anticipate energy demands, prepare for extreme weather, and understand factors affecting electricity generation, this partnership will support a more reliable and resilient energy system.

“Sound energy planning depends on models that reflect real-world conditions,” said Virginia Energy Director Vince Maiden. “This collaboration will help us better understand how weather affects electricity supply and demand, identify vulnerabilities, and weigh resource tradeoffs with greater confidence.”

The partnership will infuse relevant NASA Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) data products into Virginia Energy’s modeling and analysis system. The POWER information supports energy generation system designs and prediction of energy production using validated data products from NASA’s Earth Science to Action program. Those key NASA products represent research and development across NASA including Langley, Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley.

Through a digital pipeline, Virginia Energy can connect to Langley’s POWER web platform to download specific datasets and put them directly into their modeling tools. NASA’s POWER team members will work with Virginia Energy researchers to streamline the exchange, adjust formats, and evaluate the need for additional data.

This new partnership was fostered through NASA Langley’s Strategic Partnerships Office that connects industry, academia, and other government agencies with center facilities, capabilities, specialized test environments, and technical expertise to bring ideas to life.

articles.title: PHP is in the foundation of 70% of websites – here’s what it is and why a flaw in the software is a major hacking threat
articles.dek: Governments and organizations around the world began scrambling on Oct.
paragraphs: Governments and organizations around the world began scrambling on Oct. 21, 2026, to fix a vulnerability in software that runs their websites, a bug that could give hackers access to data and control of websites. The flaw in PHP, the programming language that powers much of today’s web, prompted urgent warnings from the U. S. National Security Agency , cybersecurity agencies and software vendors.

A researcher at Calif , a security research firm, found the flaw in August 2026 using an advanced artificial intelligence model from OpenAI. The firm alerted the nonprofit that manages PHP. However, word of the flaw leaked before the PHP organization released patches for its software, and according to Amazon Web Services officials, hackers began “broadly” attempting to exploit it .

The vulnerability has implications far beyond a single company or platform, because PHP is a key piece of software that helps run millions of websites. So, what is PHP, what role did AI play in uncovering the vulnerability, and should the average user worry?

PHP is a programming language that powers most websites . For a modern website to provide dynamic content, visual elements and searchable features, a program must run on the web server and take user input, whether that is entering a web address or clicking links and buttons. Estimates suggest that around 70% of websites run on PHP.

PHP operates on a web server in two main parts : the core PHP system – the engine and runtime libraries – and the individual PHP scripts, which are the custom programs that actually implement a website. When you interact with a website, PHP scripts run, take user input and produce the output your web browser displays.

The current security issue sits directly in the core PHP system and the libraries it uses. When a vulnerability exists at this deep level, it can allow an adversary to exploit the system. In this case, they can run unauthorized commands on the computer hosting the website, which allows attackers to access data and gain full control of the website.

This vulnerability is not a mistake in an individual website’s code. The issue lies in the core PHP system, making every unpatched system running PHP vulnerable. Since websites are accessible to anyone on the internet, adversaries can easily find PHP-based websites using automated tools. From there, they can run an exploit program that takes advantage of the vulnerability.

This exploit code is called PHP2Shell. This name comes from the fact that the exploit gives the attacker “shell access,” a cybersecurity term for direct command-line control of the computer running the website. Shell access bypasses the website interface, giving adversaries a window to enter commands and access all the website’s data.

What makes this vulnerability particularly interesting is how it was discovered. This exploit came to light through a process known as coordinated disclosure, in which cybersecurity researchers report the flaw to PHP developers before publicizing it.

This discovery shows the power of AI in cybersecurity. For decades, finding subtle software flaws required large teams of specialists manually reviewing code. Today’s AI systems can examine vast codebases and identify unusual patterns in hours or days. These models can analyze millions of lines of code in seconds, spotting subtle memory management bugs that human auditors might miss over decades of software development. The PHP vulnerability has existed in the core PHP code for over a decade, and AI helped researchers find it.

However, this also shows that attackers can use these same tools to locate and exploit vulnerabilities. The same reasoning capabilities that help security researchers find flaws first can also let attackers rapidly scan the web for vulnerable targets and automate the creation of tools to exploit the vulnerabilities.
This illustrates why it is so critical for security teams to use AI to find vulnerabilities and report them safely and actively. AI can also help release patches that mitigate these vulnerabilities .

Many government agencies, universities, hospitals and businesses rely on PHP-based systems . While individual internet users are unlikely to be directly affected, organizations that delay patching could expose sensitive data, risk having their operations disrupted or give attackers a foothold into larger networks.
PHP runs entirely on remote web servers. If you are an everyday internet user visiting websites, you do not need to download a patch or fix your personal computer.

However, if you manage a website, blog or server, even a small site built on popular content management systems such as WordPress, you should check your server administration panel or web host immediately to ensure your PHP software is updated to the latest patched version. If a third party hosts your website, check with them to see whether they have patched for these vulnerabilities.

The PHP2Shell discovery illustrates a new reality for cybersecurity. In our interconnected world, keeping web infrastructure secure is a continuous race. As AI tools become standard for both cyber defenders and online adversaries, maintaining fast patching habits remains our most essential defense.

articles.title: A Cave Full of Ancient Human Remains Has a Strange Secret: Where Are All the Males?
articles.dek: Ancient tooth proteins raise the possibility that Homo naledi, an extinct human relative, reserved a burial site for females, hinting at complex customs once thought unique…
paragraphs: Ancient tooth proteins raise the possibility that Homo naledi, an extinct human relative, reserved a burial site for females, hinting at complex customs once thought unique to modern humans.

For more than a decade, researchers have wondered why the adult fossils in South Africa’s Dinaledi Chamber look so much alike. The remains of Homo naledi , an extinct relative of modern humans, show almost none of the physical variation expected between males and females. Ancient proteins extracted from teeth found in the chamber now suggest a possible explanation: the sampled individuals may all have been female.

The chamber lies within the Rising Star Cave system, where Homo naledi was discovered in 2013. The species lived between 335,000 and 241,000 years ago and possessed an unusual combination of primitive, ape-like traits and human-like features.

To investigate the lack of variation, researchers from the University of York, the University of Copenhagen, and more than 10 other international institutions recovered the first ancient proteins from Homo naledi fossils. Their study, published in Cell , examined the largest extinct hominin population yet studied through protein analysis.

The team used a minimally destructive acid-etching technique to extract microscopic protein fragments, called peptides, from the enamel of 23 teeth representing at least 20 individuals. They looked for Amelogenin-Y, a protein encoded by a gene on the male Y chromosome, but found no trace of the male marker.

To check that the recovered proteins were genuinely ancient rather than modern contamination, a team at the University of York’s specialized chemistry facility analyzed their amino acids, the molecular building blocks of proteins.
Palesa Madupe, who completed the work as part of her postdoctoral research at the University of Copenhagen, explained why tooth enamel can preserve evidence that other skeletal material may lose.

“Unlike those found in other remains like bone fragments, proteins in tooth enamel are preserved because dental enamel – the hardest tissue in the human body – shields proteins from environmental contamination even for millions of years.

“This makes them ideal carriers of genetic information from deep time. Our study helps in the long-standing mystery of why Homo naledi lacked significant variation; it’s probably because they could have all belonged to one sex.”

If the Dinaledi Chamber was a burial site reserved exclusively for females, it could represent the first known example of sex-specific burial by a species other than Homo sapiens . Such a practice could imply complex, symbolic treatment of the dead previously thought unique to modern humans, raising questions about how Homo naledi organized its society.

Dr. Marc Dickinson, from the University of York’s Department of Chemistry, said, “The lack of male markers with the group is truly fascinating. It is incredibly exciting to gain a window not only into the biology of our ancestors, but also into how they lived.

“These findings offer rare insights into a culture that has, until now, been difficult to access directly. Advances in ancient protein analysis are opening the door to a far richer and more nuanced understanding of ancient hominins.”

The absence of Amelogenin-Y does not, however, establish that every sampled individual was female. The researchers also identified a possible biological explanation. If the Homo naledi population was highly isolated, the gene encoding the protein could have mutated or been deleted. Males could therefore have been present in the chamber, with teeth that lacked the usual male marker.

articles.title: Why ultra-Orthodox parties hold so much sway in Israeli politics
articles.dek: On Oct. 20, 2026, a week before Israel’s elections, dozens of men were detained on suspicion of evading the draft – arrests that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called…
paragraphs: On Oct. 20, 2026, a week before Israel’s elections, dozens of men were detained on suspicion of evading the draft – arrests that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called “unacceptable .”

The young men attend ultra-Orthodox, or Haredi, religious schools, whose students were long exempt from the military service mandatory for most Israelis. A 2024 court ruling that Haredi men must be drafted alongside other Jewish youth intensified the conscription debate. Netanyahu’s government has failed to either legalize the draft exemption or enforce the court’s ruling, though he has said Haredim who are not studying should enlist .

With Israel’s military fighting in several conflicts, those exemptions have become increasingly unpopular: The vast majority of Jewish voters want Haredi communities to share the burden . Haredi political parties, however, are key potential coalition members as Netanyahu attempts to secure his political future. Although a relatively small percentage of the population, the Haredim hold disproportionate sway in Israel’s parliamentary system.

Haredi Jews strictly observe Jewish religious law and often disapprove of liberal interpretations. They typically live in Haredi-majority neighborhoods where large families are the norm – six children, on average – and about half of the men devote themselves to full-time religious study . The poverty rate is 33% , more than double the percentage for non-Haredi Jews.

The Israeli public is about 14% Haredi , but the community is growing quickly because of its high birth rate. Projections by the Central Bureau of Statistics estimate that almost a quarter of Israelis will be Haredi by 2050.

Haredi communities are diverse and represented by two main political parties. Haredim who are Ashkenazi – Jews whose ancestors came from northern and eastern Europe – are linked to United Torah Judaism, or UTJ. Those who are Sephardi or Mizrachi, meaning their ancestors came from the Iberian Peninsula and the Middle East, are linked to Shas.

A third Haredi party, Haredi Public, was formed in July 2026 . The party says it will represent Haredim who feel underserved by Shas and UTJ , emphasizing employment and poverty, housing development and the education system. Unlike the other two Haredi parties, it has included women on its candidate list.

Elections for the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, use a proportional representation system . Any party that receives more than 3. 25% of votes receives seats based on the fraction of votes it received. Each party allocates its seats to members based on a list of candidates published before elections.

Having multiple parties with similar target demographics risks dividing the vote, leaving that group with fewer representatives in the Knesset. Shas and UTJ have agreed to share their surplus votes in the 2026 election to maximize their overall seat share.

Because of the low electoral threshold, many parties are able to win seats. No Israeli party has ever attained the 50% share needed to control parliament by itself. As in other countries with similar systems, it is very common for parties to form coalitions and govern as a team.

Likud, one of the major conservative parties, has led most governing coalitions for the past two decades , with party leader Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister. Haredi parties are seen as strong conservative allies , and they have been key coalition members for Likud administrations. Today, as Netanyahu faces challenges from other right-wing parties over his handling of Oct. 7, 2023, and several wars, Likud may need them even more.
The fact that Likud has needed Haredi parties to form coalitions has given them negotiating power. For many years, one of their priorities has been draft exemptions for religious education .

Military service is mandatory for most groups in Israel, although Muslim and Christian Arab citizens are generally exempted. Jewish Israelis see conscription as a unifying experience and a costly demonstration of commitment to the state. Starting at age 18, most women serve two years and most men serve almost three years. Former soldiers can be called up as reservists into their 40s, depending on their training.

For decades, Haredi men received de facto exemptions. It was, effectively, one of several government arrangements that subsidize Haredi communities. Religious schools for teen boys and married men receive government payments for each student. Given the communities’ low employment rates, large families and high poverty rates, many families rely on public support .

In 2024, Israel’s Supreme Court ruled that a blanket exemption from military service for Haredim was not legal . Netanyahu’s government struggled to enact a compromise between those who favored drafting Haredim and the Haredi parties; the failure to find a lasting legal way to exempt Haredi men led Shas and UTJ to leave the Likud-led coalition in 2025.
Nonetheless, this ruling has not led to mass conscription.

Haredi groups have held public protests , and many have ignored draft notices. While tens of thousands of men are draft eligible but not serving , and most of them are Haredi, fewer than 500 evaders have been arrested in 2026. Netanyahu argues against arrests , saying they discourage men from enlisting without coercion.

In July 2026, at the urging of Haredi parties, the government passed a law to temporarily prevent arresting draft evaders. Some members of Netanyahu’s governing coalition opposed the law, however, and right-wing opposition parties filed petitions to challenge it in court .

Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett – leader of the Together alliance, and seen as a key contender to oust Netanyahu – has threatened to cut subsidies to the Haredi community if they continue to defy the draft. Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, is another top contender to replace Netanyahu . He has proposed allowing 3% of Haredi men exemptions to study , while drafting the majority.

As the number of conflict zones increases – Gaza, southern Lebanon and Iran, as well as deployments in the West Bank – the unequal burden of military participation is a growing source of resentment among many conscripted Israelis and their families. Seven in 10 Jewish Israelis favor drafting the Haredim.
Shas and UTJ, however, have declared they will not join a coalition unless it promises to codify the draft exemption into law .

When the Haredi parties exited Netanyahu’s coalition, Likud replaced them with nationalist parties that emphasize the state and Jewish supremacy. Particularly notable was the decision to include the Jewish Power party , an offshoot of an earlier group banned for racism ; including Kahanist groups was long seen as a red line .

Haredi communities, on the other hand, tend to prioritize religious Jewishness over the state. Most Haredim do not consider themselves Zionist , and a small percentage are anti-Zionist . They argue that it was sacrilegious for people to create a state of Israel rather than waiting for God to return Jews to the land of Israel. Where nationalist politicians emphasize the secular state and military service, Haredim see their religious study as service to the Jewish community.

As Likud’s changing coalition shows, Netanyahu’s alliances are strategic rather than ideological. I believe his decision to side with the Haredim on the recent draft legislation suggests his coalition is open to revision after the October 2026 election.

articles.title: Common Chemicals Trigger Alarming Changes in Human Breast Tissue Models
articles.dek: Chemicals that disrupt hormones may leave a molecular “scar” that could someday help identify people at higher risk of breast cancer, research in human breast tissue models…
paragraphs: Chemicals that disrupt hormones may leave a molecular “scar” that could someday help identify people at higher risk of breast cancer, research in human breast tissue models suggests.

People are typically exposed to several chemicals at once, including endocrine-disrupting chemicals that can interfere with the body’s hormones. Scientists have increasingly questioned whether these exposures contribute to breast cancer risk. Much of the evidence, however, comes from animal models or laboratory-grown cells that cannot fully reproduce the complexity of human breast tissue.

Researchers at Tufts University School of Medicine and Boston University investigated those effects using three-dimensional models of normal human breast tissue called organoids. Their study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences , found that three common bisphenols, BPA, BPS, and BPF, produced relatively few changes when tested individually. When combined at very low concentrations comparable to levels detected in human blood and urine, the chemicals disrupted normal development in organoids from most of the tissue donors.

The organoids were grown from breast tissue donated by 13 healthy young women. They contain multiple types of breast cells and can reproduce some aspects of human breast tissue development, allowing researchers to examine chemical exposures during that process.

“The breast also is unusual in that it undergoes major developmental changes well after birth, including during puberty and pregnancy,” said Charlotte Kuperwasser, the study’s senior author and a professor of developmental, molecular, and chemical biology at Tufts University School of Medicine. “And the concern is that breast tissue cells may be highly sensitive to environmental cues, such as chemical exposure, during critical windows of mammary gland development.”

As the organoids developed over about three weeks, the team exposed them to individual chemicals and mixtures. The panel included substances that disrupt hormones, chemicals that affect metabolism, and known or suspected carcinogens. Researchers then analyzed changes in gene activity and DNA modifications. Different chemicals affected development in different ways, with the bisphenol mixture producing the most striking finding.

“We intentionally used concentrations of chemicals that were relevant to real-world exposure rather than the very high doses sometimes used in toxicology studies,” said Kuperwasser. “We also tested a mixture of these because people are typically exposed to multiple chemicals at the same time.”

To explore how the changes associated with the bisphenol mixture might relate to disease, the team compared them with molecular data from human breast cancers. The exposure-associated pattern was most strongly represented in data from patients with invasive lobular carcinoma, a type of breast cancer that may not produce a detectable lump and can be difficult to detect with a mammogram.

That resemblance does not establish that the chemicals cause cancer or explain how the observed changes might contribute to breast disease. The researchers instead describe the work as a new way to investigate how environmental exposures affect normal human tissue before cancer develops.

“Historically, we have thought about cancer risk largely in terms of inherited mutations, lifestyle factors, and exposures that directly damage DNA,” said Kuperwasser. “These findings raise another possibility: Environmental exposures may subtly alter how normal tissues develop, leaving behind molecular changes that do not cause cancer by themselves but may make the tissue more permissive to cancer many years later.”

Kuperwasser noted that persistent molecular changes could eventually serve as a biological record, like a “scar” of past exposure. If validated in people, such markers could potentially help identify individuals at higher risk of breast cancer and guide earlier or more targeted screening.
“If these results are validated by additional studies, they could change how we think about cancer prevention,” said Kuperwasser.

Studies involving larger and more diverse groups of donors, along with a broader range of chemicals and mixtures, are needed to determine how widely the findings apply. Researchers also need to establish whether the molecular changes seen in organoids persist in human tissues and whether they are associated with, or contribute to, breast disease later in life.
